Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment marked by moderating inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and supply chain challenges, while remaining focused on executing our strategic priorities like premiumization, innovation-led growth, and operational agility.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Michael to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Rivera:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.8 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year, or 4.2% on an organic basis excluding FX headwinds and divestitures. Gross margin was 52.8%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, driven by pricing discipline, supply chain productivity, and favorable mix shifts. Operating income rose 11.4% to $2.1 billion, with adjusted operating margin at 15.2%. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42 adjusted, up 13%, and free cash flow was outstanding at $1.8 billion. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives, including $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a 7% dividend increase.

Let me start with our organic sales growth rate, which remains the north star metric for assessing the underlying health of our $28 billion global CPG business across snacks, beverages, household care, personal care, beauty, food, and health & wellness. Organic sales grew 4.2% year-over-year in Q3, accelerating from 3.1% in Q2 and ahead of our 3-4% guide, outperforming the CPG industry average of 2.8% per NielsenIQ. Volume contributed 2.1%, price/mix 2.0%, and distribution a modest 0.1%, reflecting balanced demand amid easing inflation.

By segment, Beauty & Personal Care at 35% of sales grew 6.8% organically, with 3.5% volume from premiumization in our FreshGlow skincare—our Dove-like clean beauty disruptor gaining 140 basis points of U.S. mass market share to 12.4% ACV via 98% natural ingredients and recyclable packaging. Price/mix added 3.3% through EDLP resets countering private label like Walmart's Equate. Food & Snacks, 40% of mix, hit 3.9% growth with 1.8% volumes and 2.1% price/mix; QuickBite savory snacks grew 9% on Sriracha Lime innovation, expanding to 78% ACV in North America and improving NGV to +2.5%. Health & Wellness was at 2.1%, with flat volumes offset by 2.1% price/mix in VitalFuel protein bars, e-commerce now 22% of sales via DTC subscriptions.

Regionally, North America at 55% of sales surged 5.6% organically on 2.9% volumes and 4.2% household penetration per IRI, outpacing P&G and Unilever with U.S. share up 60 bps to 8.7%. Europe was 1.8% amid palm oil regs and weak sentiment, but we protected margins with +15 bps NGV. Emerging Markets excelled at 7.4%, led by 15% growth in NutriGlow vitamins in India and Brazil on urban expansion and 500 new POS. FX shaved 1.2% off reported growth, mitigated by 85% local-for-local sourcing.

This reflects our Power of Three: innovation with 22% of sales from <3-year-old products via AI flavor profiling boosting QuickBite trials 18%; supply chain via $150 million Project Horizon cutting COGS 120 bps; and 4,500 global distribution points in Amazon Fresh and DoorDash. For Q4, we see 4-5% organic growth with volumes to +2.5% on holidays. Risks include protein inflation up 3% QoQ and Nestlé's nutrition push, but 14% EBITDA margins, $1.2 billion FCF, and 2.5x net debt/EBITDA support $400 million repurchases.

Diving deeper into pricing actions, which have been pivotal against inflation in our categories. We achieved 4.2% net revenue growth with +6.1% price/mix offsetting -1.9% volumes—third straight positive quarter despite industry softness like PepsiCo and Unilever. Selective 5-8% list price hikes in snacks and household care, e.g., 7% MSRP on TrailMix bars and CleanWave detergents in North America (45% revenue) to counter 12% YoY palm oil and surfactant costs. Our AI elasticity modeling from BlackCurve simulated 50,000 scenarios, targeting inelastic segments; ASP rose 6.3% driving 80 bps NRG uplift, volumes down just 1.2% vs. category -2.8%, maintaining 92% ACV and 1.4 units/store week velocity with 15% TPG cuts vs. Great Value.

Trade promotion reset cut spend 20% of revenue, shifting to push promos like BOGO-50% on Quench beverages; in EMEA, 10% higher thresholds on GlowEssence shampoos vs. Aldi/Lidl, yielding +5.4% price/mix, 110 bps MMS in UK grocery per Kantar, and ROPI to 3.2x from 2.4x—adding 120 bps to 48.2% gross margin. Premiumization gave +2.3% mix via Organic TrailMix and EcoClean; in APAC (25% revenue), 12 premium SKUs at 10-15% premiums on Tmall/Flipkart with -0.4 elasticity drove +7.8% NRG, flat volumes vs. 4% category drop, gaining 1.5 share points via 8% COGS cuts from reformulation and lightweight PET.

LATAM (15%) saw 9% pricing counter 25% hyperinflation for +11.2% price/mix despite -4.5% volumes, mitigated by micro-pricing in bodegas at 85% distribution. North America resilient at +4.1% NRG, elasticity to -0.7. Cooling cocoa -15% QoQ held 20% portfolio steady like Nestlé. Our Profitable Growth Framework prioritizes price/mix; $50M in pricing tech including Walmart dynamic pilots. Q4 +5% price/mix for FY24 4-5% NRG and 75 bps MMS.

On gross margin guidance, we reaffirm FY2024 at 52.5-53.5%, +150 bps vs. FY2023's 51.2%; Q4 53.0-53.5% on holiday strength. Q3's 52.8% expanded 210 bps on prestige mix like Lumina skincare +15% in NA and +4.2% AUR. Pricing: +350-450 bps from 5.5-6.5% AUR growth, elasticities resilient per 10,000 household panels; NA 6-8% on fabric/oral care vs. 28% private label, EMEA 7-9%, APAC/LATAM 4-6%/8-10%. Input inflation -200-250 bps at 3.5-4.5% (packaging +5%, cocoa +10%, labor +4%); 70% hedged, Brent $75-80/bbl. Productivity +300-400 bps via $1.2B Elevate 2027: Q3 $150M from 15% beverage yields, facility consolidation, RSPO palm unlocking rebates. Mix/volumes +50-100 bps on premium clean beauty 60%+ margins, e-comm 18%; FX neutral to -50 bps. Confident in upper half for 53%+ by FY2025.

Before shifting, a note on competitive activity. Industry faces 2.1% CPI inflation, private label at 28%, DTC rise. In NA (52% sales), P&G Tide Bio-Concentrate grabbed 2.1 pts laundry share vs. our Whirl (-0.4 pt to 28.1%); Unilever Dove Men+Care +4 pts drug ACV; Great Value/Simple Truth +7% cleaners. We responded with 8% Whirl Pods investment reclaiming 1.2 pts, +1,500 linear feet to 96.2% ACV, AI promo mgmt improving ROI 18%. Europe (28%): Reckitt Dettol Eco-Refill +3.5 pts, Henkel Persil -1.8 pts BioClean to 24.3%, Aldi/Lidl 31% fabric care. EcoShield PFAS-free 98% biobased debuted 85% EMEA grocery, +14% velocity. APAC/LATAM: P&G Olay AI +2.7 pts China facial, Colgate Max White -1.1 pts Brazil. $100M Dada Nexus dark stores reversed DTC losses, VitaFresh +3.1 pts LATAM informal. 12% revenues to shopper marketing, ML predicts pricing ahead, M&A eyed for pet food.

Following my remarks, Lisa will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent Crunch for Good campaign, which boosted Gen Z household penetration by 22% in snacks via sustainability messaging. We've optimized trade spend, improved ROPI, and leveraged data analytics for personalized efforts—our machine learning on loyalty data lifts conversions 30%, with AR try-ons driving 15% of new product trials digitally. E-commerce now 22% of sales, DTC bundles on gcb.com enhancing personalization and velocity.

After me, David will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

David Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. In Q3, these efforts delivered $42 million in savings, year-to-date $128 million or 12% better than prior year—85 bps gross margin accretion offsetting 8% YoY palm oil/PET inflation from SE Asia weather and Red Sea reroutes.

Procurement yielded $18M or 6% of spend via 15% supplier rationalization with Cargill/Indorama; AI dynamic sourcing cut NA raw materials 4.2%, shifting 20% tropical oils to soy de-risking geopolitics like Unilever/P&G. Manufacturing: $14M from OEE 93.2% +250 bps across 45 plants; cobots in 12 facilities +18% throughput on Crunch bars/PureThirst, Mexico SMED -22% changeovers, EMEA IoT predictive maintenance clawed €25M amid EU regs. Logistics: $10M from 16% ocean freight cuts with Maersk, intermodal rail 30% U.S., warehouse automation 70% DCs lifting turns to 9.2x compressing WC $220M; Singapore AMRs -11% fulfillment for Shopee/Lazada, Colombia nearshoring -60% Brazil port costs.

These build resilience: Scope 3 tracking -14% transport emissions via FourKites, ahead of Colgate in ESG. Reinvesting 2-3% COGS into precision fermentation pilots. FY savings $175M +15%, GenAI demand sensing -25% forecast error. Supports 100-150 bps op margin expansion despite tariffs.

Finally, Elena will share insights on our innovation pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, David. We are excited about the progress on new product development. Our pipeline is robust, and innovations will drive future growth. Our recent Radiant Earth Glow Serum is showing promising early results, capturing 8% premium serum share, 65% ACV drug channels, 42% e-comm sales at 35% margins via Ginkgo biotech.

In Q3, 17 new SKUs generated $285M incremental sales or 14% of growth, +22% YoY, 25% higher repeats per IRI. EcoShield Pods $112M, 12% UK penetration stealing 2.5 pts from Domestos, 78% repurchase. VitaFuel Bites $67M, 18% convenience velocity.

Pipeline 2026 with $450M R&D +15% YoY: 40% sustainability, 30% health, 30% digital. Q4: 12 SKUs like HydraBloom Mist, PureAir Refresher, KetoCore Shakes. 2025: 28 SKUs, CBOS 2.0 personalization for MyBlend powders, $200M run-rate YE26.

NA 16% growth contribution omnichannel, Europe 11% regs-aligned, APAC 28% VitaFuel India, EM 19% value premium. Shrinkflation-proof, 35% clean-label, 45% recycled packaging. $1.8B incremental 2025 sales. Recent $150M BioFerment acquisition accelerates.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for submitting questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Alex Johnson with Morgan Stanley.

Alex Johnson:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

David Patel:
Thanks, Alex. Absolutely, packaging waste reduction is core to our sustainability and efficiency goals. Through value engineering and lightweight PET initiatives, we've cut 8% of COGS in 30% of portfolio, with EcoShield Pods using 100% plant-derived recyclable materials aligning with EU PPWR—reducing waste while boosting margins 25%. Our TerraCycle partnerships enable closed-loop recycling, and AI sourcing has shifted to 40% recycled content, yielding $18M procurement savings including 5% from supplier negotiations. Year-to-date, this contributes to our $128M total savings, with warehouse automation further compressing inventory obsolescence by 30%. We're on track for 60% recycled by 2030, unlocking retailer rebates and positioning ahead in ESG.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs.

Maria Lopez:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

Lisa Chen:
Great question, Maria. Data analytics is transforming our marketing. Our CBOS 2.0 uses ML on 500M+ loyalty points from Kroger and apps for tailored campaigns—e.g., QR scans for MyBlend custom supplements boosting conversions 30%. TikTok Shop and AR try-ons drive 15% new trials, 22% e-comm sales with 25% velocity uplift. In APAC, Tmall personalization reversed DTC losses; NA Crunch for Good Gen Z targeting +22% penetration. Promo ROI up 18% via NielsenIQ AI, dynamically allocating to high-elasticity SKUs for 2.1% organic ex-FX.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

Michael Rivera:
Thanks, David. Commodity increases like cocoa +10%, palm flat but historical 8% YoY, and PET/labor +4-5% pose a -200 to -250 bps headwind, but our 70% hedging covers 60%, Elevate productivity +300-400 bps more than offsets for 52.5-53.5% FY guide. RSPO palm at 2% premium unlocks rebates, dual-sourcing mitigates volatility; we've locked 80% cocoa at $4,200/ton. Q4 seasonal mix and 5.5-6.5% pricing keep us at upper end, even with Brent $75-80.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays.

Emily Carter:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Johnathan Hale:
Emily, thanks for the question. Competition is intense with private label at 28% +200 bps, DTC disruptors, and branded moves like P&G Tide/Persil, Unilever Dove/Reckitt. We've held/gained share via precision responses: 8% Whirl investment reclaimed pts, EcoShield premiumization +14% velocity EMEA, $100M dark stores APAC. Trends like sustainability (68% millennial resonance) and health halo favor our 45% recycled/35% clean-label pipeline. CPG Velocity Engine predicts pricing, 12% shopper marketing protects 85% list prices. Q4 share stable, holiday upside from omnichannel.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Johnathan for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy—delivering 6-7% organic growth FY24, mid-teens EPS CAGR to 2027 via Peak Horizon, 50 bps annual margin expansion to 18%, ROIC >20% through high-velocity factories, premium health M&A, portfolio shaping. Our indispensable brands position us to outperform in value-seeking times. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
